text:
A: Hello? Can you hear me alright? Sorry, I'm never quite sure if it's working.
B: Yeah, I can hear you.
A: Oh good, thank goodness. I'm Joanne, I'm in Gosport, down near Portsmouth. Erm, I don't really know what we're meant to talk about, do you?
B: Not really. Just chat, I think. I'm Ryan. Castleford.
A: Castleford, is that up north, love?
B: Yeah, West Yorkshire. Near Wakefield.
A: Oh lovely. I've never been up that way, I don't get about much, I sort of stay local. What do you do, if you don't mind me asking?
B: Mechanic. Small independent garage. Servicing, brakes, MOTs and that.
A: Oh, that's ever so handy. My sister Michelle's always saying she wants someone she can trust with her car. She had her clutch done last year and she was convinced they ripped her off, you know, she came round mine nearly in tears about it.
B: Happens a lot, to be fair. Clutch is a big job though. It's mostly labour. What'd she pay?
A: Erm, I think it was about six hundred?
B: Bit steep. Not mad though. Depends on the car.
A: Well, that's made me feel better for her, I'll tell her that. Sorry, I'm rabbiting on. Do you like it, the job?
B: It's alright. Pays the bills. Mostly. Mad busy at the minute, everyone's MOTs are due at once.
A: Oh I bet. I work in a school kitchen, a primary. Eleven years now. Food prep, serving at lunchtime, washing up, wiping down the hall after. I know all the kiddies, which ones have allergies, which ones won't touch a pea. There's one little boy who'll pick every single pea out and line them up on the side of his plate, bless him.
B: Ha. My girlfriend works at a nursery. She says same. Kids and food.
A: Oh does she? Ah, that's nice. What's her name?
B: Chloe. She likes it. Knackered all the time though.
A: Oh, I know that feeling. My knees are terrible on cold mornings, I sort of creak in through the door.
B: I'm on me feet all day an' all. Under cars. Back's not great.
A: Oh, you're too young for a bad back, love! Erm, what did you make of that puzzle thing at the start? I was useless. I love a jigsaw, but that one, I just went to pieces.
B: Didn't finish it. Ran out of time.
A: Oh, thank goodness, I thought it was just me.
B: Do you do jigsaws then?
A: Oh, all the time. Thousand-piece ones, countryside scenes mostly. The one I've got on the go now is a nightmare, it's all sky, just blue and more blue. And my cat Biscuit likes to sit right in the middle of it, so I'm forever lifting him off and finding bits stuck to his fur.
B: We've got a dog. Bruno. He'd eat a jigsaw. He chewed one of Chloe's shoes last week.
A: Oh no! Was she cross?
B: Bit. It were a new one. He weren't bothered.
A: They never are, are they? Biscuit knocked my tea over Tuesday and just looked at me. Erm, what do you do of an evening then, after work?
B: Walk the dog. Have me tea. PlayStation. That's about it really.
A: That sounds nice and quiet. I have my dinner and put The Chase on, that's my evening. I don't know if that's very exciting, sorry.
B: Me mam watches that. Shouts at it.
A: Oh, I shout at it too! Don't tell anyone. Does your mam get many right?
B: More than me, to be fair.
